purpose: Chlorambucil is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat certain types of cancer, including chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and some types of lymphoma. It helps slow down or stop the growth of cancer cells in your body. Your doctor may also use it for other conditions involving an overactive immune system.
how_it_works: Chlorambucil works by interfering with the DNA inside cancer cells, which stops them from being able to copy themselves and grow. Think of it like putting a wrench in the machinery that cancer cells use to multiply. Because it damages the cell's blueprint, the cancer cells eventually die off.
common_side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, and stomach upset are common, especially when you first start taking it. You may also notice a decrease in your blood cell counts, which can make you feel tired, increase your risk of infections, or cause easy bruising and bleeding. Mouth sores and loss of appetite can also occur.
warnings: This medication can seriously lower your immune system, making it harder to fight infections — call your doctor right away if you have a fever, chills, or signs of infection. It can harm an unborn baby, so use reliable birth control during treatment and do not breastfeed. Long-term use may slightly increase the risk of developing another type of cancer. Never take more than prescribed, and keep all follow-up blood test appointments so your doctor can monitor your counts closely.
typical_dosing: Dosing is very individual and depends on your weight, kidney function, and the condition being treated. It is usually taken by mouth as a tablet once daily or in short cycles as directed by your oncologist. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions and never adjust the dose on your own.
